schemes.official_name: Global TIES (ENG 100D Design for Development / ENG 100L Design for Development Lab)
schemes.description: Interdisciplinary undergraduate teams design, build, test and deliver solutions for local or global nonprofit/NGO partners. ENG 100D includes a group project for a nonprofit; ENG 100L is the long-term lab for accepted Global TIES students.
schemes.admin_host: Jacobs School of Engineering / Center for Global Sustainable Development
schemes.eligible_faculties_programmes: ENG 100D open to all undergraduates; ENG 100L restricted to applicants accepted into Global TIES
schemes.eligibility_restrictions: ENG 100L by application and department approval; ENG 100D prerequisite CAT 2/DOC 2/HUM 2/MCWP 40/MMW 2/WCWP 10B/SYN 1
schemes.credit_assessment: ENG 100D 4 units; ENG 100L 2 units, repeatable six times
schemes.project_evidence: ENG 100D: 'Includes a group project designing a solution for a local or global nonprofit organization' [1]; ENG 100L: teams 'design, build, test, and deliver solutions to real-world problems' [1].
schemes.employer_evidence: Catalog states group project is 'for a local or global nonprofit organization' and 100L students work with nonprofits and their communities [1]; search summary of Global TIES site says teams work with an NGO on a real-world problem [2]. Nonprofit's role in supervision/feedback/receipt of output not verified on a fetched page (Global TIES site pages returned 404 to WebFetch).
schemes.partner_role: Nonprofit/NGO partner for whom solution is designed; long-term community partners for 100L
schemes.named_partners: Spring 2026 project list per search summary: Schoolhouse Ghana, Diabeatit!, Cruz Roja (Tijuana) [2]
schemes.latest_evidenced_year: Spring 2026 project list (search summary only); catalog current
schemes.unresolved: Global TIES site pages not fetchable; partner role in assessment/feedback not directly quoted; catalog page undated year (UCSD current catalog).

profile_md: UC San Diego has one university-wide, partner-set team route and several programme-level routes. **i4X** (The Basement) puts multidisciplinary graduate/undergraduate teams on challenges supplied by regional and national partners (JLabs, City of San Diego, San Diego Zoo) over two quarters, with partner check-ins; the Winter/Spring 2027 cohort is recruiting. **Global TIES** (ENG 100D open to all undergraduates, ENG 100L by application) has teams design solutions for nonprofits/NGOs; the legacy row is reassessed here, with partner role evidenced mainly by catalog wording. In business, the **Rady Action Project** (MBA teams of 4-6, about 8 weeks) and the **MSBA Capstone** (teams of 3-5, 10 weeks, 28 companies in the cited year) work with named companies; RAP's year and required status are not shown. Engineering (MAE 156B, Bioengineering BENG 187/188, ECE) and data science (DSC 180A/B) have sponsored team capstones, but sponsors include UCSD faculty and units, so external connection is only Unclear. GPS catalog courses mention client teams without current evidence. Nothing was verified for natural sciences, arts/humanities or health. Where clients are internal UCSD units (e.g. MAE 156B faculty sponsors) they do not satisfy the employer criterion.
gaps: Global TIES site pages returned 404 to WebFetch (partner role evidenced via catalog and search summary). Rady RAP/MSBA pages undated for RAP; required status unknown for RAP, MSBA, MAE 156B, DSC 180. ECE 191 and BENG 187/188 not separately recorded; further departmental capstones likely. TIES (Sixth College), GPS client courses, USP community courses unverified. Natural sciences and health sciences not found/searched; HDSI industry page and 70+ projects figure only from search summary.
